entities.summary: Trinidad and Tobago is a sovereign nation in Caribbean, Americas. Its capital is Port of Spain. Official languages include English. Government: Unitary parliamentary constitutional republic. Population: approximately 1.5 million. Area: 5,131 km². Comprehensive index for Trinidad and Tobago covering Arawak/Karinepagoto/Kalina indigenous, Columbus 1498, Spanish colony (Trinidad de la Santísima Trinidad), British conquest 1797, sugar/cacao economy, African slavery then Indian indentured labor (1845-1917, ~145,000, largest per capita Indian diaspora), oil discovery 1907, independence 1962, Eric Williams PNM dominance, Black Power movement 1970, coup attempt 1990 (Jamaat al Muslimeen), ethnic politics (Afro-Trinidadian PNM vs Indo-Trinidadian UNC), and Carnival/calypso/steelpan global influence.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Trinidad and Tobago's independence in 1962 marked a significant milestone for the Caribbean region, as it became the first country in the area to gain full independence from British colonial rule. This event had far-reaching consequences for regional politics and identity.
